fatal_errors: The hypothesis omits the temperature-dependent governing mechanisms central to the target: cryogenic inertial dulling from reduced phonon drag and high-temperature Portevin–Le Chatelier pinning by diffusible Mn- and Fe-rich atmospheres.

It treats nominal atomic-size mismatch as interchangeable with measured or calculated local lattice distortion/MSAD, although composition-dependent chemistry and magnetism can make these quantities diverge.
No prior evidence is supplied despite the explicit request for supporting evidence.
explanation: The response recovers one important component of the target: local lattice distortion impedes dislocation glide, and a controlled composition series with direct distortion measurements could test whether greater distortion correlates with higher strength. Its single-phase-solid-solution boundary and falsification concept are scientifically reasonable. However, it is only a partial reconstruction. The target used oriented FCC single crystals, temperature-dependent CRSS, strain-rate jumps, TEM, and DFT/MSAD to distinguish three regimes: thermally activated solid-solution glide, low-temperature inertial dulling, and high-temperature dynamic solute pinning. The generated hypothesis instead proposes generic tensile tests from room to moderate temperature, predicts work-hardening changes not established by the target, and does not specify the relevant temperatures, strain rates, slip system, or CRSS normalization. Composition changes also alter chemistry and elastic or magnetic properties, so merely comparing high- and low-size-mismatch alloys would not uniquely identify lattice distortion as the cause. Direct correlation of CRSS with independently measured MSAD under matched single-crystal conditions would be more discriminating.
